description: Localized shared words and names (character names and game terms) stored as directly fetchable GameText rows and as the <GLO=KEY> substitution dictionary for GameText and SystemText tags.

ID.simple: Glossary term ID (row key), e.g. GLS_GAME_WORDS_....
ID.technical: FName ID of FGameDataTableRow_GameText. Runtime FindRow matches the DataTable row name, not this field; all 314 row keys equal their ID value in all 11 exports. The same loaded UDataTable is placed first in AGameTextManager::TextDataTables (index 0 of the 14-table array) and read by Tick to add Row->ID.ToString() as a key in GlossaryParameters (an FGameTextParameterMap of FString keys to shared string parameters) for <GLO=KEY> substitution in FormatText. Character and other data rows point at GLS_ ids through FName fields; the glossary is not loaded twice: one loaded asset is used both as TextDataTables[0] and as the sole source of the parameter map. The language-suffixed asset is GlossaryTextDataTable_<EApplicationLanguage name>; the 11 exported suffixes are De, En, Es, Es_LA, Fr, It, Ja, Ko, Pt, Zh_Hans and Zh_Hant.

Text.simple: The localized word/name substituted for <GLO=ID> tags or displayed directly for a GLS_ id.
Text.technical: FString row text (+0x10), the second and last reflected field. The row constructor sets no explicit defaults, so an empty export value is an empty string. GetGameText copies this field after the first matching row is found; a missing row also yields an empty FString. Tick adds its value to GlossaryParameters with EGameTextParameterOptions::None. FormatText uses the glossary map for recognized <GLO=KEY> tags (the tag pattern admits digits, uppercase A-Z and underscore) and replaces the whole match with the parameter's ToString output, including any tag modifiers; unresolved keys leave the tag untouched. A plain glossary value is not recursively formatted. DYN=FRIEND_WORD / DYN=FREND_LIST_WORD in Zh_Hant/Zh_Hans are instead injected as text-id parameters pointing at GLS_GAME_WORDS_3000 / GLS_GAME_WORDS_3004, which resolve through GetText (nested lookup) when ToString runs. Empty glossary strings produce empty substitutions. All 11 shards have 314 rows: 19 empty values in De, En, Es, Es_LA, Fr, It, Ja and Pt, and 12 in Ko, Zh_Hans and Zh_Hant (the same 12 IDs in every shard). There are no numeric units or table-level sentinel values.

notes: All 11 exported language variants share the same 314 row IDs, and every row key equals its ID. This group is both a normal GameText table (the glossary asset is element 0 / the first of the 14 tables in TextDataTables, so GLS_ ids can be requested directly) and the sole source of GlossaryParameters. StartLanguageLoading requests GlossaryTextDataTable_<Language> through GamePrimaryAssetType_DataTable; Tick waits for all loaders, resolves the loaded UDataTable through the asset-manager cache, rebuilds TextDataTables while skipping null pointers, adds/overwrites every glossary row, and only then broadcasts OnCultureTextLoaded (GameTextManager.cpp:547-577). Tick empties only a local copy of GlossaryParameters, not the member; because all shards have identical IDs, every key is overwritten on a language change.

Direct data relationships: CharacterDataTable Id_GlossaryText_Name and Id_GlossaryText_StoryName, CharacterSpecialAttackDataTable Id_GlossaryText_Name, BannerDataTable Id_BannerMessage and MapDataTable Id_MapText are FName fields that contain GLS_ ids. GLO tags in BattleText, ItemText, CommandList, Tutorial and SystemText resolve through this table; every GLO key referenced by the available exports exists in the 314-ID set, and no GLO tag modifiers occur in the exports.

Dispatch and precedence: IsSystemTextId tests a case-insensitive SYS_ prefix; all other ids (including GLS_) search the 14-table GameText array in order, and the first matching row wins, so a duplicate GLS_ row in the first glossary table shadows later tables. FindRow is called with bCheckNone=false. DYN text-id parameters call GetText and can reach the glossary indirectly; GLO always reads GlossaryParameters, never the request parameters.

Widget path: IGameWidgetTextSettingInterface::SetTextIdOnly immediately builds a request and calls GetText through SetTextRequest, then stores TextId and parameters; StudioLocalization2 re-resolves those cached ids on a language change. GameCharacterSelectPlayerInfoWidget.cpp:268 therefore performs an immediate lookup, not a deferred one. Direct manager calls also occur in GameCharacter.cpp:900 and GameOnlineManager.cpp:2752. Consumer fallbacks are SYS_SYMBOL_0004 for NAME_None and SYS_COMMON_LABEL_0042 for CP_000 or a missing character row in select/lobby widgets; collection and visual-lobby code uses the same system ids when no character row is found. A missing glossary row for a direct GLS_ id returns empty text rather than one of those fallbacks.

Reconstruction caveat: the glossary repopulation is part of AGameTextManager::Tick, which is behaviour-certified rather than byte-identical (status/functions.json 0x14c96f0; BEHAV BG03); FormatText is byte-matched (0x14c4870). Only partial Content is available and Blueprint-only uses are not asserted.

usages.detail: Requests GlossaryTextDataTable_<Language> through the DataTable primary-asset loader and installs the resolved pointer as the first entry of the 14-table TextDataTables array.
Adds every row as key = Row->ID.ToString(), value = Row->Text, options None; only a local copy of the map is emptied, and OnCultureTextLoaded fires after all rows are added.
FormatText sends <GLO=KEY> lookups to the glossary map and leaves unmatched keys as literal tag text; tag modifiers are applied through the parameter's ToString.
GetGameText finds the first GameText row in table order and copies its Text; no row produces an empty FString before formatting.
ApplyCharacterSetup falls back to the character row's Id_GlossaryText_Name only when Setup.DisplayName is empty.
In the online path that switches a character to AI control, assigns the active character's glossary display name.
For chat category 20 with a valid character and target, adds TARGET as a text-id parameter for the target's Id_GlossaryText_Name on BTL_HUD_LABEL_0508.
SetTextIdOnly resolves immediately through GetText and caches the id/parameters; StudioLocalization2 re-resolves the cached request with the new language.
Uses SYS_SYMBOL_0004 for NAME_None, SYS_COMMON_LABEL_0042 for CP_000, and the character row's glossary id only after a successful character-row lookup.
Directly requests the hard-coded GLS_GAME_WORDS_1110 glossary row through the text manager.
In Zh_Hant/Zh_Hans, DYN=FRIEND_WORD and DYN=FREND_LIST_WORD become text-id parameters for GLS_GAME_WORDS_3000/3004, whose ToString performs a nested GetText lookup.
